sections.markdown:
**Think of GS1 Digital Link as turning every barcode into a smart URL.**

A classic EAN-13 barcode carries a GTIN — a number the CASH REGISTER understands but the CONSUMER can't use with a smartphone. GS1 Digital Link changes this: instead of the barcode encoding just `8901234567895`, it encodes `https://id.gs1.org/01/08901234567895`. Scanning this URL:

- **Consumer** — opens a webpage with product info, recipes, allergen alerts, promotions.
- **Retailer POS** — parses `/01/` to extract the GTIN → same behavior as an old barcode.
- **Regulator** — parses batch + expiry + serial from URL path to verify authenticity.
- **Brand owner** — one QR / DataMatrix carries all use cases; server-side redirects route each scanner to the right destination.

URL structure: **`{host}/{primary AI}/{primary value}[/{qualifier AI}/{value}...][?{data AI}={value}...]`**

- Primary: GTIN (`/01/`), GLN (`/414/`), SSCC (`/00/`).
- Qualifiers: variant (`/22/`), lot (`/10/`), serial (`/21/`).
- Data: expiry (`?17=YYMMDD`), best-before (`?15=YYMMDD`), weight (`?310n=`).

**Why every consumer-facing packaging in 2026+ ships this:** the retail industry (Sunrise 2027) is migrating all EAN-13s to 2D codes with GS1 Digital Link inside. Consumers point their phone at a milk carton → info page loads. Pharma DataMatrix carries GTIN + batch + expiry + serial in Digital Link form → regulator scans same code → verifies authenticity.

**GS1 Digital Link** is a URI standard for encoding any GS1 identifier + qualifiers + attributes into a well-defined web URL structure. Structure: `{scheme}://{host}/{primary AI}/{primary value}[/{qualifier AI}/{qualifier value}...][?{data AI}={data value}&...]`. Compatible with QR + DataMatrix + NFC + human-readable. Resolves via **GS1 Resolver** — configurable redirect service that routes scans to different destinations based on scanner context (consumer app, retail POS, regulator).

## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Random-order AIs.** Path order MATTERS — primary AI first, then qualifiers. Data attributes go in query string.
**Mistake 2: URL-encoding text values incorrectly.** Batch `ABC/123` breaks the path; percent-encode.
**Mistake 3: Storing GTIN inconsistently in URL.** Padding rules: `01` slot expects GTIN-14 padded; parsing must normalize.
**Mistake 4: Bypassing the resolver.** Hardcoding brand.com/product/X means you can never route different scanners differently. Always resolve.
**Mistake 5: Not caching resolver responses.** Every scan hits the network → slow + expensive. Cache with TTL.
**Mistake 6: Forgetting DataMatrix + QR need FNC1 in classic AI form** but Digital Link URLs don't. Encoding rules differ.
**Mistake 7: Assuming ALL scanners understand URI form.** Legacy POS may only parse classic AI syntax; support both.
**Mistake 8: Storing PII in URL query.** Digital Link is often publicly scannable; DON'T leak identifiers or coupons that could be replayed.
## Best practices
**1. Ordered path AIs** — primary + qualifiers in canonical order.
**2. Percent-encode text values.**
**3. Resolver-based routing** — flexibility.
**4. Cache resolver responses** with sensible TTL.
**5. Support classic + URI syntax** — dual scanners.
**6. Analytics on scan context** — count consumer vs retail POS scans.
**7. HTTPS only** — never http.
**8. Structured data on resolved pages** — schema.org Product markup for SEO + search.

## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What problem does GS1 Digital Link solve that classic barcodes don't?**

**A:** Classic barcodes (EAN-13, GS1-128, DataMatrix with classic AIs) encode structured data that ONLY specialized scanners understand — the CONSUMER's phone has no idea what to do with `(01)08901234567895`. Digital Link turns the same data into an HTTPS URL: `https://id.gs1.org/01/08901234567895`. Consumer phones parse it as a URL, load a product page. POS still parses `01/…` for the GTIN. Same barcode serves both worlds. **Also:** ONE code carries GTIN + batch + serial + expiry + attributes; one QR / DataMatrix carries the whole story. Combined with the industry's 'Sunrise 2027' — plan to replace EAN-13 with 2D codes — Digital Link is the migration destination for retail packaging. Interviewer signal: knowing it's not just a URL trick but an industry-wide migration.

**Q2: How is a Digital Link URL structured?**

**A:** `{scheme}://{host}/{primary AI}/{primary value}[/{qualifier AI}/{qualifier value}...][?{data AI}={data value}&...]`. **Primary AI** — the main GS1 key: `01` (GTIN), `414` (GLN), `00` (SSCC), etc. **Qualifiers** are AIs that make the primary MORE SPECIFIC: `10` (batch/lot), `21` (serial), `22` (variant). Multiple qualifiers stack in canonical order. **Data attributes** in the query string are optional metadata: `17` (expiry), `15` (best before), `3103` (net weight kg). **Order matters** — the primary comes first; qualifiers follow in canonical order; data goes to query string. Interviewer bonus: knowing WHY the split — path AIs form the identifier; query AIs are attributes.

**Q3: What is a GS1 Resolver + why use one?**

**A:** A **Resolver** is a redirect service that takes a Digital Link URL + scanner context and serves a specific destination. Same URL, different consumers: a shopper's phone gets recipes; a retailer gets stock info; a pharmacist gets verification data; a regulator gets traceability. **Config-driven** — brand owners define routing rules in the resolver dashboard; no need to reprint packaging when the destination changes. **Standard Resolver format** — GS1 publishes a spec for how routing decisions are made based on `Accept-Language`, `linkType` query param, User-Agent. **Cost saver:** one packaging print serves many use cases across the product's lifetime; can add campaigns without new SKUs. Interviewer red flag: 'I'd hardcode the URL' — misses the whole point.

**Q4: How does Digital Link handle both classic AI syntax + URI syntax?**

**A:** Some scanners are legacy — they only parse classic AI element strings like `(01)08901234567895(10)BATCH99`. Others are modern — they parse the URI form. A **dual-encoded barcode** carries BOTH: the primary payload is a Digital Link URL that contains the classic AIs in URL-parseable form. Scanners choose their preferred parse path. **On the app side:** your scan handler should try URL parsing first (Digital Link) → fall back to classic AI parsing. **In DataMatrix encoded via ISO/IEC 15434**: format-05 for the URL form; format-04 for classic. **This dual-support is critical during the migration years** — Sunrise 2027 doesn't mean every scanner is upgraded overnight. Interviewer signal: knowing the migration reality.

**Q5: How do you handle percent-encoding + AI value rules in URLs?**

**A:** Values must be **URL-safe**. Text AIs (batch, lot, serial) can contain characters like `/`, `?`, `#` that break URL parsing → percent-encode (`%2F`, `%3F`, `%23`). GS1 spec restricts allowed characters — check the AI's allowed set. **Numeric AIs** — GTIN in `01` slot is 14 digits padded; date AIs use `YYMMDD`; weight AIs use fixed-decimal implied (e.g., `3103` = kg × 10⁻³). **Case sensitivity** — AI values ARE case-sensitive in most cases (batch `abc123` ≠ `ABC123`). **Duplicate AIs** in the same URL — invalid; each AI appears once. **Interviewer signal:** knowing encoding rules + not just 'stringify the value.'

**Q6: How would you build a consumer Flutter app that scans + resolves Digital Link codes?**

**A:** **(1)** Camera scan via `mobile_scanner` — configure QR + DataMatrix formats. **(2)** On detect, parse raw string: if starts with `https://` → try Digital Link parse; else → classic AI parse. **(3)** Extract GTIN + qualifiers + attributes. **(4)** If Digital Link URL, follow the resolver (HTTP GET with `linkType` context) → get canonical product URL. **(5)** Render product page in WebView OR fetch structured data via API + native UI. **(6)** Cache resolver responses to Hive with 24h TTL. **(7)** Offline mode: match against a local product catalog by GTIN. **(8)** Analytics: track scan → resolve latency + destination clickthrough. **(9)** Handle regional resolvers (id.gs1.org global; id.gs1india.org for India-specific). This is the flagship Consumer 2027 pattern; senior interviewers respect the full pipeline.

## Real-world usage

- **Consumer QR on packaging** — Coca-Cola, Nestlé, Kellogg's already deploying.
- **Pharma DataMatrix** — GTIN + batch + expiry + serial in Digital Link URLs.
- **GS1 India products** — many brands migrating.
- **Recall management** — resolver switches destination to recall page.
- **Anti-counterfeit** — serial + resolver verify authenticity.
- **NOT ideal for** — internal SKUs (use plain identifiers).

## Advanced notes

- **`linkType` query param** — specify desired destination type (`gs1:pip`, `gs1:productBundle`, `gs1:recipeInfo`, `gs1:certificationInfo`).
- **`Accept-Language` header** — resolver serves localized destination.
- **Fragment id** — reserved by GS1 for future use.
- **Digital Link Toolkit** — open-source parsers + validators in multiple languages.
- **Cache-Control on resolver responses** — respect TTL for perf.
- **Legacy Web** — some old browsers can't handle DataMatrix scan → paste URL into address bar; support that fallback.
- **NFC tags** — same Digital Link URL can be written to NFC — tap-to-scan alternative.
- **Web NFC on mobile Chrome** — reads NFC tags with URL payloads → same handler.
- **Print-on-demand** — some retailers dynamically generate Digital Link labels at checkout.
- **API vs URL** — resolvers can return JSON structured data instead of HTML redirects (linkType = `gs1:linkset`).
- **Testing** — GS1 provides a Digital Link Validator + Toolkit online.
- **Regulatory** — EU + India + regulatory frameworks are aligning on Digital Link for consumer transparency.
